subject: English
introduction: Paragraph cohesion questions test your ability to organize ideas logically, choose the right transition words, identify where sentences belong, and spot structural weaknesses. A well-organized paragraph has unity (one main idea), coherence (logical flow), and cohesion (grammatical/lexical connections between sentences).

key_formulas.name: Contrasting
key_formulas.formula: \text{however, nevertheless, on the other hand, yet, although, despite}

key_formulas.name: Cause-Effect
key_formulas.formula: \text{therefore, consequently, as a result, thus, hence, because}

key_formulas.name: Sequence
key_formulas.formula: \text{first, then, subsequently, finally, having done X}

key_formulas.name: Exemplification
key_formulas.formula: \text{for example, for instance, such as, namely, to illustrate}

key_formulas.name: Concession
key_formulas.formula: \text{admittedly, although it is true that, granted that}

tips_and_tricks: The topic sentence is usually first — it introduces the paragraph's main idea.
Look for pronouns (it, they, this, these) — they must refer to something already introduced.
Addition connectors (moreover, furthermore) = same direction as previous point.
Contrast connectors (however, on the other hand) = opposite direction.
Cause connectors (because, since, as) introduce explanations.
A sentence that contradicts the paragraph's main idea doesn't belong — this tests 'Which sentence should be removed?'
For 'best placement' questions: test the sentence before and after each option; check pronoun reference and logical flow.

worked_examples.title: Example 1: Choosing the right transition
worked_examples.question: The study revealed that students who slept fewer than 6 hours scored significantly lower. _____, those who slept 8+ hours performed above average.
solution: Step 1: Sentence 1 = sleep-deprived students score low.
Step 2: Sentence 2 = well-rested students score high.
Step 3: These are contrasting outcomes, so a contrast connective is needed.
Step 4: 'In contrast' or 'On the other hand' fits best.
Step 5: 'Furthermore' would be wrong because the second sentence isn't adding to the first — it's contrasting.

worked_examples.title: Example 2: Finding the sentence that doesn't belong
worked_examples.question: Read: (1) Exercise improves cardiovascular health. (2) Regular physical activity strengthens the heart and reduces blood pressure. (3) Walking is a low-impact form of exercise. (4) The economy has grown by 4% this year. (5) Even thirty minutes of daily activity can produce health benefits. Which sentence does NOT belong?
solution: Step 1: Identify the main topic: exercise and cardiovascular health.
Step 2: Sentences 1, 2, 3, 5 all relate to exercise and health.
Step 3: Sentence 4 ('The economy...') is completely unrelated to the topic.
